More than half the quality-eligible candidate pixels are excluded by the requested separation; unselected imagery and quality exclusions are reported separately.

Blocks are randomly assigned across a two-dimensional grid; whole patches are removed symmetrically only near a different active split. AOI edges, nodata/quality exclusions, and seams within the same split do not create buffers. Quantization and both-sided removal can produce a gap larger than requested.

The paired training comparison keeps buffered validation/test patches fixed. Its restored-training baseline still inherits the heldout side of the symmetric buffer; inspect its actual separation rather than assuming it fails the requested guard.
